title: Identity read request v1
description: `fgos identity pins` lists the machine keys this machine pinned: the first key seen for a machine id is remembered in user state (<stateRoot>/identity/pins/<machine-id>, never in a repository) and a different key claimed for that machine is refused `machine-key-changed`; the answer is {pins: [pin]} ordered by machine id; each pin is `seen` or `confirmed` (`fgos identity pins --confirm`, an identity.write operation). `fgos identity machine` also prints `keyFingerprint`, the `SHA256:` fingerprint of the machine signing key minted by `fgos doctor --fix` (null while no key can be read). `fgos identity machine`, `fgos identity session`, `fgos identity project`, `fgos identity resolve <handle|lead:LANE|full id>` and `fgos identity list [--project]`. Read-only: never mints, never writes. `resolve` answers the one live session of the local directory (<stateRoot>/identity/sessions/) that the handle, role alias or full id (`<machine-id>/<local id>`) names, or is refused `not-found` or `ambiguous` with the candidates in the message (Identity's own codes; the mailbox maps them to its own names; only when it has no answer does it ask the shared directory: the sessions other machines published through the Event Store of this clone's project (stream project:identity, events identity.session-published and identity.session-ended, each signed by its machine and verified against its pinned key). A remote answer has liveness `remote`, `machine`, `fetchedAt` (the clone's last fetch) and `pin`, and a full id of another machine resolves through it; without a project id or a migrated Event Store a full id of another machine is `not-found`), and in `candidates` of the `--json` refusal; `list` answers `{sessions, pruned: 0}`, oldest registration first, only the sessions of this repository's project id with `--project`. `machine` answers the machine id, its handle and its alias; `session` answers this session's full id and handle. A refusal (exit 65, no envelope) names its reason: machine-id-missing when no machine id was minted, unresolved when the caller cannot be told from any other. `project` answers the project id, handle and creation time read from the tracked file .fgos/project.json of the main checkout (also from a linked worktree); a refusal names project-id-missing when no id was minted, project-id-unreadable when the file is not valid, not-a-repository outside a git repository, git-read-failed when the repository cannot be read.
x-stateRoot: the fgOS state root (FGOS_STATE_ROOT, else the holder-lock resolution); files machine-id and machine-alias; under identity/ the signing key machine-key (mode 600) and machine-key.pub, and pins/<machine-id>
x-projectFile: .fgos/project.json of the main checkout: {v: 1, projectId: 32 hex, handle: Convention project-handle, createdAt}

refusal.title: Identity refusal under --json
refusal.description: What stdout carries when the verb is refused and the caller passed --json: one line, exit 65, the same text on stderr as `fgos: error: <error> [<reason>]`. It is not a fgos.v1 envelope (no `contract`): the error path is not wrapped, success and failure differ by exit code. `reason` is one of the outcome's x-refusals.

candidates.description: The sessions the caller may have meant (not-found), the sessions a name matches (ambiguous), the live sessions holding the role (role-not-held); empty otherwise. A candidate of another machine also carries machine, fetchedAt and pin, and the liveness value remote; consumers ignore unknown fields.

state.description: seen until the owner confirms the fingerprint; a file without state reads as seen

confirmedAt.description: present only when state is confirmed

clone.description: Working directory the session registered from.

liveness.description: unknown: the session has no terminal ancestor, so nothing can prove it dead. remote: a session of another machine, never claimed alive. A dead session is never returned.

machine.description: Only on a remote session: the machine that published it (its id when another machine shares its handle).

fetchedAt.description: Only on a remote session: when this clone last fetched other machines' events; absent when it never did. The entry is as fresh as that.

pin.description: Only on a remote session: how far the publishing machine's signing key is trusted.
